scope: finite single-process snapshot WAL retention and resumable RBU update

setup: CREATE TABLE item(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,label TEXT,qty INTEGER)
mutations: UPDATE item SET label='changed',qty=111 WHERE id=1
snapshot.read: SELECT id,label,qty FROM item ORDER BY id

targetSetup: CREATE TABLE item(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,label TEXT,qty INTEGER)
updateSetup: CREATE TABLE data_item(id INTEGER,label TEXT,qty INTEGER,rbu_control)
CREATE TABLE rbu_count(tbl TEXT PRIMARY KEY,cnt INTEGER) WITHOUT ROWID
rbu.read: SELECT id,label,qty FROM item ORDER BY id
rbu.indexRead: SELECT id,label FROM item INDEXED BY item_label WHERE label>='c' ORDER BY label,id

limits: Single process with sequential connections; no threads, races, sleeps or failure injection.
Snapshot handles belong to one live WAL generation. A pinned read transaction retains history; no compare/open after WAL deletion or close.
snapshot_recover runs outside a read transaction on the live WAL; orphaned/PERSIST_WAL recovery is not covered.
RBU uses a rollback-journal target, ordinary INTEGER PRIMARY KEY rows, one secondary index, explicit separate state database and default VFS.
RBU vacuum, custom VFS/rename, deltas, virtual tables, constraints, interrupted-process recovery and concurrent writers remain separate.
Exact rows and finite state/progress traces are established by the separate pinned native oracle, then compared by generated application bodies.
